references.text: Moses' father-in-law Jethro is mentioned earlier in the chapter, providing context for their meeting.
Jacob bowed to Esau when they met, a similar gesture of respect that Moses showed his father-in-law.
Laban kissed Jacob when they met, a parallel to how Moses kissed Jethro as a greeting.
Esau kissed Jacob when they were reunited, similar to the affectionate greeting between Moses and Jethro.
Joseph asked about his brothers' welfare (shalom), just as Moses and Jethro asked each other about their well-being.
Samuel asked if Jesse's family was doing well (shalom), the same type of polite expression found in the meeting between Moses and Jethro.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent, similar to how Moses brought Jethro into the tent after their meeting.
Parallel greeting (kiss) confirming unity and reunion after separation.
Typological parallel: A kiss as a sign of restored relationship after separation.
